Module/Program Information

The MOS Co-op Program aims to provide 4 – 16-month practical degree-related experience in a paid employment setting. All students enrolled in a four-year undergraduate degree program with an Honours Specialization, Specialization, or Major in the BMOS program at King’s University College are eligible to enroll in the MOS Co-op Program.

Students must also satisfy the eligibility requirements which are to: (i) be registered in full-time* academic studies at King’s University College in a BMOS program and (ii) be in good standing with their program module as appropriate. International students are eligible to apply for the program.

Students interested in the MOS Co-op Program should apply through Western Connect (http://connect.uwo.ca). Students apply to the program in the fall of each year to complete a 4-month work term. Students enrolled in a 20.0 course degree program may apply in the Fall term of their third year of study to complete between two to four consecutive 4-month work terms.

Students who meet the academic eligibility criteria will be required to attend preparatory workshops and meet other requirements included in Management and Organizational Studies 3996A/B/Y prior to their first work term. Students who are successful in securing a 4-month co-op will pay a fee and receive 0.5 course credit for Management and Organizational Studies 3996A/B/Y upon successful completion of the first work term. Students who are unsuccessful in securing a co-op will be withdrawn from Management and Organizational Studies 3996A/B/Y without academic penalty and will not be liable for the co-op fee.

Students who secure a second 4-month co-op and meet the requirements of Management and Organizational Studies 3997A/B/Y will pay a fee and receive 0.5 course credit for Management and Organizational Studies 3997A/B/Y upon successful completion of the second work term. Students who are not successful in securing a co-op will be withdrawn from Management and Organizational Studies 3997A/B/Y without academic penalty and will not be liable for the co-op fee.

Students who secure a third 4-month co-op will pay a fee and achieve the “MOS Co-op Program” themed program upon successful completion of the third work term. Students can complete a maximum of four 4-month work terms and achieve a maximum of 1.0 course credit.
Each four-month work term will be recorded on the Academic Transcript with a course notation:
Work term 1 – Management and Organizational Studies 3910A/B/Y
Work term 2 – Management and Organizational Studies 3920A/B/Y
Work term 3 – Management and Organizational Studies 3930A/B/Y
Work term 4 – Management and Organizational Studies 3940A/B/Y
A co-op fee will be charged for each 4-month work term.
Students who qualify to receive a continuing scholarship in the academic year in which they participate in the MOS Co-op Program are permitted to defer receipt of the scholarship for one year.

Students may not take any academic courses during the co-op work term courses, unless granted special permission by the Associate Academic Dean. Only those students with a cumulative average of at least 75% should apply for special permission.
Participating students will continue to have access to the student health plan while on work term.
*Students registered with Accessible Education are considered full-time if enrolled in 40% of a full-time course load (i.e., 1.0 course or more per term).
